_comment: Martial Hero by LuizMelo -- Creative Commons Zero (CC-0). Licence text is
in LICENSE.txt beside this file; provenance is in docs/ASSETS.md.
Frames are 200x200 throughout. The character occupies roughly 80px of that,
with its feet near y=120 -- hence anchorY, which is what stops the fighter
floating above the floor or sinking through it.
An attack's three phases are three sub-ranges of ONE file, because that is
what a Commitment Window is: one animation sliced by the frame data.
attack1.png is 6 frames -> startup 0-1, active 2-3, recovery 4-5, which is
why a viewer can watch a punish land during the recovery tail.
special-active and special-recovery deliberately overlap on frame 4:
attack2.png has 6 frames and the phases need 3+2+2, so the recovery tail
re-uses the last active frame rather than the pack being padded with a
block has no dedicated animation in this pack. `fall` is the braced,
arms-raised pose and reads as a guard; it is the closest honest match, and
a pack that ships a real block should point this clip at it.
